titleEn: I Did It. I Am Sorry!

pages.text: "Grandpa, there is a hole in my boot!" Nils the little bear held up one boot. A round hole was right at the toes. By the stove, Grandpa Bruno put on his glasses.
"Tomorrow I want to run and run in the snow!" Nils hugged the boot. "I will mend it." Grandpa took off his glasses, put them on the table, and looked for thread. Excited, Nils ran around the room.
While circling, Nils stepped on something on the floor. Crack! Grandpa's glasses had fallen from the table. One arm snapped off.
Nils felt hot right to the tips of his ears. He quickly picked up the glasses and pushed them under the covers. Then he sat by the stove, pretending nothing had happened.
Grandpa felt around on the table. "Oh, where are my glasses?" Nils glanced at the covers and kept his mouth tightly shut. The boot with the hole still lay beside the stove.
His heart felt heavy, as if a stone were resting on it. The stove fire grew smaller, and Nils felt no joy at all. "I did it. I am sorry..." he whispered to himself.
Nils gripped the covers, then slowly lifted them. He held the broken glasses in both paws and offered them to Grandpa. "Grandpa, I did it. I am sorry!"
Grandpa took the glasses and patted Nils's shoulder. "Thank you for telling me. We can tie this with thread." He wrapped thread around the broken arm, and the glasses rested on his nose again.

With his glasses on, Grandpa carefully stitched the hole in the boot. "One, tell right away! Two, show what happened! Three, fix it together!" Nils raised both paws above his head. "The hole is gone!"
Grandpa sat Nils on his lap and gently stroked his back. Hiding makes your heart heavy; telling lets you fix things together. "I did it. I am sorry. And thank you for mending my boot!"
